title: Completed clearance stays completed after an office reopens it
problem: Adding an unpaid Bookstore obligation returns the Bookstore signature but leaves the overall clearance marked COMPLETED.
simple: A student can still look fully cleared after the school records a new unpaid obligation.
steps: In the isolated fixture, complete every office and set the clearance to COMPLETED. Sign in as Bookstore. Submit add_bookstore_obligation for that student with an amount of 100. Inspect both the clearance and Bookstore station rows, then reopen the student dashboard.
expected: Either reject changes to a finalized clearance with a clear policy, or reopen the overall record and invalidate affected downstream approvals consistently.
actual: The real POST returned 303. Bookstore became RETURNED while clearances.status remained COMPLETED with completed_at populated.
evidence: SC-009 in scenario-tests.json; source shows the student completion flag trusts overall COMPLETED even when office counts disagree.
root: The new-obligation handler changes only the office record. There is no shared downstream revocation/overall-status reconciliation.
fix: Define one transactional revocation rule, apply it to reopened obligations and downstream signatures, and derive completion from consistent authoritative records.
impact: Incorrect final clearance and contradictory student/office records.
verification: Reproduced through the actual HTTP handler and verified in the synthetic MySQL database.

title: Registrar-created CBE clearances are stuck between Organization and Dean
problem: The normal Registrar initializer makes Dean pending and Organization locked for CBE, although CBE Dean approval requires Organization/YBC approval first.
simple: Each office waits for the other, so a newly enrolled CBE student cannot get started.
steps: Create a synthetic CBE enrollment and call prepareSemesterClearanceRecords(), as the Registrar flow does. Read the station statuses. Attempt Organization approval and then Dean approval with assigned synthetic staff.
expected: Organization PENDING, Dean LOCKED, and Organization/YBC can begin the CBE sequence.
actual: Organization was LOCKED and Dean PENDING. Organization reported that Dean must approve first; Dean reported that CBE Organization/YBC approval is required first.
evidence: SC-001. Existing CBE suites passed because they use startStudentClearance(), a different initializer that handles CBE specially.
root: Registrar initialization and semester opening hard-code DEAN as the first station. The legacy student initializer uses a college-specific first station.
fix: Use one authoritative college-specific initializer for preparation, semester opening, and any legacy entry path. Test newly generated CBE records, not just migrated records.
impact: Blocks the real CBE clearance journey.
verification: Reproduced with actual application functions and saved station rows.

title: An unauthenticated test URL changes office readiness data
location: tests/readiness_test.php:8, :46, :53; tests/ directory has no HTTP denial rule
problem: A database integration test is executable through the web without login and performs real readiness mutations.
simple: Someone who has not signed in can run a developer test against the school's data.
steps: Use only the isolated server: set its semester to PREPARING and place synthetic notes on NOT_READY offices. Request /tests/readiness_test.php without a cookie. Compare the notes afterward. Do not repeat this against the school database.
expected: HTTP 403 or 404 with no database changes.
actual: HTTP 200 returned a passed-test message; a Student Council readiness note became NULL. The live Apache also exposes /tests/ and executes the harmless navigation regression without login.
evidence: SC-008; TC-115 and TC-116. Actual mutation was demonstrated only on synthetic records.
root: Several integration tests lack a CLI-only guard, and the deployed tests directory is web-accessible.
fix: Exclude tests from the served document root or deny HTTP access to the entire directory; also enforce CLI-only execution in database-mutating scripts.
impact: Unauthorized state changes, lost notes, test data creation, and unexpected processing load.
verification: Reproduced unauthenticated mutation in the isolated deployment; harmless live exposure check confirmed. No persistent staff-session bypass was observed in the separate bulk-render helper.

title: Single Dean approval verifies an evaluation that was never submitted
problem: Individual approval automatically marks CCS faculty-evaluation requirements VERIFIED instead of requiring an independently verified result.
simple: The approval button can turn missing evaluation evidence into a verified requirement.
steps: Create a synthetic CCS clearance with NOT_STARTED evaluation requirements and no evaluation submission. Sign in as its Dean or invoke approveDeanClearance() with that assigned synthetic Dean. Inspect the Dean and requirement records.
expected: Under the supplied specification, approval is rejected until evaluation verification is complete.
actual: With zero proof submissions, Dean approval succeeded and the requirement was marked verified during approval.
evidence: SC-003; individual and ready-only bulk paths use different prerequisite behavior.
root: The individual approval path treats the Dean's click as verification; the readyOnly checks do not apply to the ordinary individual path.
fix: Require a trusted verification result before signing, or explicitly approve and document a separate manual-attestation policy. Keep individual and batch eligibility consistent.
impact: Evaluation requirements can be satisfied without the evidence required by the supplied specification.
verification: Reproduced with actual application functions and saved MySQL state. This is also a policy conflict with the current manual-confirmation design.

title: Library can approve a student who still has a borrowed book
location: clearance/office_workflow.php:58 and :279; library dashboard uses the shared eligibility rules
problem: Library eligibility checks the card status but does not check outstanding borrowed_books rows.
simple: A verified library card can be enough to clear a student even while a book is still out.
steps: In the isolated database, give a student a VERIFIED library card and a borrowed_books record with status BORROWED. Make Library PENDING. Call the actual eligibility and approval functions.
expected: The outstanding book prevents approval and is explained to staff/student.
actual: Eligibility was true and Library became APPROVED while the book remained BORROWED.
evidence: SC-005. The fixture explicitly inserts a verified card; an earlier fixture that omitted that row was corrected before final results were recorded.
root: Borrowed-book obligations are absent from Library list, eligibility, and generic approval checks.
fix: Include unreturned books in the authoritative Library eligibility rule and expose the blocker in the relevant interface.
impact: Unreturned school property may not prevent clearance.
verification: Reproduced with saved card, book, and station rows.

title: Open SASO discipline cases do not prevent SASO approval
problem: SASO eligibility considers its sub-check signatures but ignores OPEN violations assigned to SASO.
simple: The system can clear a student's conduct stage while an unresolved conduct case is recorded.
steps: In the isolated database, complete Organization and SASO child checks. Insert a synthetic OPEN violation at the SASO station. Make SASO PENDING and call approveOfficeClearance() for SASO.
expected: Under the supplied conduct requirement, the unresolved case blocks signing.
actual: SASO became APPROVED with the OPEN case still present.
evidence: SC-006; no SASO case-management interface was discovered, although the dashboard describes conduct review.
root: The current SASO function is a signature aggregator; a SASO violation blocker is not implemented.
fix: Agree the conduct rule, then enforce it in shared eligibility and staff/student feedback. Do not assume Computer Lab's separate violation rule covers SASO cases.
impact: The implemented conduct behavior does not meet the supplied office responsibility.
verification: Reproduced against a synthetic violation in the existing schema. The missing SASO case-management workflow is an implementation gap.

title: Dean can retrieve confidential evaluation screenshots
problem: The implementation gives the CCS Dean the original submitted image rather than only a verification result.
simple: Changing a submission's label to an anonymous code does not hide names or private content inside its screenshot.
steps: Upload a synthetic evaluation bitmap through the actual student endpoint. Sign in as the assigned CCS Dean. Request its /dean/evaluation_image.php?id=... URL.
expected: The supplied privacy requirement says the Dean receives only the necessary verified/unverified result and cannot retrieve confidential screenshots.
actual: The Dean received HTTP 200 and the original PNG bytes. The submissions page embeds and links these images.
evidence: SC-012. Only a generated nonpersonal image was used. A Library role was denied access in EX-062.
root: The current product deliberately uses anonymous manual image review by the Dean, which conflicts with the requested confidentiality model.
fix: Resolve the privacy/workflow specification before deployment. Separate confidential evidence review from Dean signing, expose only the required result, and define retention/access rules.
impact: Potential exposure of identity and confidential evaluation content to a role the supplied specification excludes.
verification: Reproduced through the authenticated image endpoint; no real student's image was accessed.

title: Apache serves Git configuration from the project
problem: The Git configuration path is publicly readable through Apache.
simple: Internal repository files are being served as website files.
steps: Send HEAD /ClearGo/.git/config to the local Apache deployment without a cookie.
evidence: TC-113. Only headers were requested; configuration contents and credentials were not retrieved.
root: No effective web-server denial covers the .git directory in this deployment.
fix: Keep repository metadata outside the served tree or explicitly deny access to version-control directories.
impact: Exposes repository metadata and may allow additional repository/history disclosure. No secret disclosure was claimed or attempted.
verification: Reproduced with a non-content HEAD request on local Apache.

title: Temporary developer scripts are inside a web-accessible directory
problem: Apache exposes the developer scratch directory, which contains scripts that connect to the application database and can apply migrations or run checks.
simple: Files intended for development can be reached as website URLs.
steps: Send HEAD /ClearGo/.tmp/. Review the local scratch scripts without requesting their mutating URLs.
expected: The scratch directory is unavailable through HTTP.
actual: The directory returned HTTP 200. Source inspection found an unguarded migration helper there.
evidence: TC-114; local source inspection of .tmp/apply-office-remarks.php. No migration helper was invoked through HTTP.
root: The Git ignore rule for .tmp does not control Apache access.
fix: Move scratch files outside the document root or deny the directory at the server level. Remove development helpers from deployment packages.
impact: Increases the attack surface and can expose operations that were never intended for normal users.
verification: Directory exposure reproduced; execution of the potentially mutating migration helper deliberately NOT TESTED.

title: New and reset accounts share a predictable initial password
location: registrar/student_import_functions.php:10 and :626; registrar/staff_action.php:44 and :87; registrar/student_action.php:57 and :119
problem: Import, account creation, and password reset use one institutional default without a required first-login password change.
simple: Knowing one new account's initial password reveals the default used for other new accounts.
steps: Run the MySQL student-import fixture in the isolated database. Verify the created account's password hash against the institutional initial value. Inspect the normal login destination and account-creation/reset paths.
expected: A new/reset account receives a unique temporary secret or equivalent activation process and must establish its own credential.
actual: The existing MySQL import test confirms the shared default is accepted. The login path redirects directly to the role dashboard, with no mandatory-change state.
evidence: Final passing student_import_mysql_test.php and student_import_scale_test.php; source paths above. No existing real account was tested with the default.
root: A shared constant is used for account passwords; the required-change policy was removed in migration 005.
fix: Use unique temporary credentials/activation and enforce first-login replacement; define safe reset and credential-delivery behavior.
impact: Accounts that retain the initial password are predictable. This is a verified configuration weakness, not a claim that a real account was compromised.
verification: Default-password behavior reproduced on synthetic imported accounts; first-login enforcement absence confirmed in source.

title: CCS and CTE use a different first office from the supplied workflow
problem: The supplied specification starts with Organization, but the current non-CBE implementation intentionally starts with Dean.
simple: The system tells some students to visit a different first office from the flow requested for this audit.
steps: Initialize a synthetic CCS enrollment through the Registrar function and read its saved station rows. Compare the configured migration order and the supplied sequence.
expected: Organization precedes Dean if the supplied sequence is authoritative for all colleges.
actual: Dean is PENDING and Organization LOCKED. The positive CCS journey completes in Dean-first order.
evidence: SC-002; JY-002 through JY-015; the initial migration and current UI agree with the implemented order.
root: An explicit specification disagreement, separate from the CBE deadlock.
fix: Have the school confirm the authoritative per-college workflow and align code, documentation, labels, and tests together.
impact: Confusing instructions and a capstone acceptance mismatch; the current CCS path itself can complete.
verification: Saved-state mismatch reproduced. Whether to change the college policy requires the project owner's decision.

title: Student evaluation uploads are accepted before clearance opens
problem: The evaluation submission backend checks active semester and Dean state but does not require clearance_status OPEN.
simple: Hiding the upload form before opening does not stop a crafted or previously opened form from submitting.
steps: In the isolated fixture, keep a student's Dean station PENDING and set the semester to PREPARING. Sign in as that student and POST a generated valid-format PNG with the student's valid CSRF token.
expected: The server rejects the student submission until clearance opens.
actual: The endpoint returned 303 and saved a SUBMITTED evaluation record while the semester was PREPARING.
evidence: SC-011. SC-004 also confirms staff approvals during PREPARING, but the current staff interface explicitly permits that; staff preparation policy is documented separately rather than mislabeled as an authorization exploit.
root: studentEvaluationContext() has no OPEN-period or current-enrollment predicate, unlike several other student upload handlers.
fix: Apply a shared student submission gate for semester state, enrollment, and station availability at the backend.
impact: Students can submit outside the period shown as available by the dashboard.
verification: Reproduced through the actual multipart upload endpoint and verified in MySQL.

title: Duplicate staff creation displays a raw database error
location: registrar/staff_action.php:118; similar RuntimeException message branches elsewhere need review
problem: A PDO exception is treated as a user-safe runtime validation error and displayed through a flash message.
simple: A duplicate email shows database language instead of explaining that the staff account already exists.
steps: Sign in as the synthetic Registrar. Submit creation of a staff account using an existing synthetic Library email. Follow the redirect to Staff Accounts.
expected: A message such as 'That school email already has an account.' Technical details go only to logs.
actual: The returned staff page contained SQLSTATE/duplicate-entry details.
evidence: SC-010. PDOException inherits from RuntimeException, so the current instanceof check is insufficient.
root: The catch branch forwards all RuntimeException messages, including database exceptions.
fix: Handle expected domain-validation errors separately from PDOException and other internal failures. Map duplicate-key conflicts to a controlled message.
impact: Confusing feedback and disclosure of internal database details.
verification: Reproduced using an actual duplicate synthetic account POST.

title: An array-shaped CSRF token triggers a raw PHP fatal error with HTTP 200
location: auth/login_process.php:12; auth/auth_check.php:198; PHP web error-display configuration
problem: The request passes an unvalidated array into a ?string parameter before the handler can reject it safely.
simple: An unusual form value makes the login page show a stack trace and internal file paths.
steps: POST csrf_token[]=invalid to /ClearGo/auth/login_process.php without credentials. No database mutation is involved.
expected: A controlled invalid-request response or friendly redirect, without warnings, paths, or stack traces.
actual: HTTP 200 text/html contained TypeError, Fatal error, auth_check.php:198, and a stack trace.
evidence: TC-107; malformed-csrf-evidence.json contains the observed response.
root: Type validation is missing at the request boundary, and the local web PHP configuration displays internal errors.
fix: Validate token shape before calling verification, handle malformed input uniformly, return an appropriate status, and log internal errors instead of displaying them.
impact: Internal implementation disclosure and misleading successful HTTP status on a failed request.
verification: Reproduced on the live local Apache using a safe invalid request.

title: Evaluation resubmission leaves the old private image on disk
problem: Resubmission deletes image references from the database but removes stored files only on the exception path, not when replacement succeeds.
simple: Old screenshots remain in storage even though the system no longer lists them.
steps: Upload one generated synthetic evaluation image, save its stored filename, then submit a replacement. Check whether the original database reference and file still exist.
expected: Superseded evidence is removed according to an explicit retention policy, or retained with an auditable reference.
actual: The old image reference count became zero while its original file remained on disk.
root: Successful replacement does not collect and unlink old stored filenames after the transaction commits.
fix: Track replacement files and clean them after successful commit, with rollback-safe handling and a defined retention policy.
impact: Unbounded storage growth and unmanaged retention of confidential evidence.
verification: Reproduced through two actual multipart submissions and a filesystem/database comparison.

title: The storage directory itself allows public directory access
problem: The storage root returns a public directory response even though its private and sessions subdirectories are denied.
simple: Internal runtime-folder structure is visible to visitors.
steps: Send HEAD /ClearGo/storage/, then compare HEAD responses for /storage/private/ and /storage/sessions/.
expected: The runtime storage root is also denied or has directory indexing disabled.
actual: Storage root returned 200; private and sessions returned 403.
evidence: TC-110 through TC-112. No private session or uploaded file body was requested.
root: Access denial is applied to subdirectories but not the storage root.
fix: Disable directory listing and deny direct access to the runtime storage tree while keeping protected image handlers available.
impact: Minor internal-structure disclosure. This finding does not claim private files are publicly downloadable.
verification: Reproduced with HEAD requests on Apache; actual listing contents were not retrieved.
